text:
B: Hiya, mate! Aneesa, is it? Did I say that right?
A: Yes, that's right. Hi. You're Mark?
B: Mark, yeah, Brierley Hill. Black Country. You're Bradford, ain't you? I saw the books in your photo and thought, she's way too clever for me, this one.
A: Ha. They're mostly novels. It's not that clever.
B: Novels! I ain't read a novel since school. Julie reads them, crime ones, on her phone. What do you do, then, are you at the university?
A: Sort of. I'm doing psychology with the Open University, part-time. And I work in a fragrance shop on Saturdays.
B: Psychology! So you're analysing me right now, are you?
A: A little bit. Only out of habit.
B: Go on then, what you got?
A: You're very relaxed for someone being filmed.
B: Ha! I am, yeah. Nothing to hide, me. I'm off work, back's gone, knee's gone. I just sit and talk to people. This is the most exciting thing I've done all week. Well, apart from the darts.
A: That's fair. I've done a few of these, actually. I like seeing how they're designed.
B: Designed, yeah? How do you mean?
A: Well, they had us rate photos first. Then we talk. Then the surveys after. I think they're checking whether you still like the people you thought you'd like. Or whether the photo was misleading.
B: Oh, that's crafty. So if I put someone down as a misery and they turn out sound, they've caught me out.
A: Basically, yeah.
B: Well I'll tell you now, I put you down as clever and you are clever, so I win.
A: Ha. Okay. What did you think of the puzzle?
B: Oh, don't. I was swearing at the laptop. Julie come in to check on me. I think I got about two right and one of them was a guess.
A: Most people guess the last few. It's probably meant to be hard.
B: That makes me feel better. Do you have to get up early for the shop, then?
A: Not that early. It's more being on my feet all day. I'm knackered by the time I get home, then I'm usually cooking tea.
B: Tea! Proper. Everyone down south says dinner. What do you cook?
A: Daal, karahi, keema. And sometimes Korean things off YouTube, which my brother and sister complain about and then eat anyway.
B: Ha! My grandkids are the same. Julie made a curry once, from a jar mind, my grandson said it was spicy and it had about as much spice as a custard cream.
A: That's a very Black Country description.
B: It is, ain't it? Slade are Black Country, you know. People think they're from Birmingham. They ain't.
A: I didn't know that. I'll keep it in mind if it comes up in a quiz.
B: It will, mate. It always does.
